page.layout: One printed page (left page of an opening, right page cut off at the edge, showing only fragments of its margin). Running text in one column with a verse couplet set apart and a marginal note at left beside the line "Objicies fortasse"; the note is a bare reference. Page number and running head at top.

main_text.p: impiam tacito agnoscunt. Increpant aliquoties Prophetæ Reges Judæ, & præ ceteris Ezekiel toto fere capite decimo septimo, quod fidem Babyloniæ regibus juratam non servassent. Locus est insignis, & quem memini alicubi Chrysostomum & fuse & pulchre admodum explicare. Quin & Gentilium historiis nobilitata est Reguli, aliorumque hac in parte fides: qui & hostibus & Pœnis (perfidissime genti) quod jurejurando intercedente promiserant, vel cum certo capitis periculo censuerint oportere præstari. Regulum hoc elogio ornat Silius, compellans eum quasi per apostrophen.

p.i: Qui longum semper fama glisscente per ævum, Infidis servasse fidem memorabere Pœnis.

main_text.p: Objicies fortasse vulgaria illa, Fallere fallentem pro fraude non habendum, & cum Cretensibus Cretizandum. Quibus addi possunt de jure bell. 13.quæ adducuntur a Grotio duo illa; alterum Bruti dictum ex Apiano

page.notes: Right-hand page is cut off at the scan edge; only a few letters of its lines are visible and were not transcribed. The marginal note at left is partly illegible; "de jure bell. 13." is a reference, read with some uncertainty. Catchword at foot of the page is shown as a mark only and was not transcribed.
